problem_type: Host approval classification guessed side effects from tool and operation names
symptom: Architecture review reproduced ten wrong approval decisions in thirteen Project Agent examples: reversible canvas/document/timeline actions were gated, undo was gated, and timeline preview was gated while the real write was allowed.
direct_cause: projectAgentExecutionPolicy.ts used hardGatePattern and safePattern regexes over renamed aliases instead of resolving the registered capability descriptor.
class_root: The Host had no shared side-effect-class invariant connecting every capability alias and operation to the approval policy, so alias renames and mixed-operation tools silently changed the safety decision.
affected_population: Project Agent Host tool calls using registered capability aliases
M2 semantic aliases and mixed-operation tools such as nomi_canvas_maintenance
Legacy and new queued turns using the step/safe-auto/project approval policy modes
internal_only_reason: This is an internal Nomi capability-contract invariant; the repository design contract and architecture review define the policy, while no third-party runtime controls the classification.
invariants: Every registered capability descriptor declares one effectClass from reversible_local, spend, or irreversible.
Host policy resolves effectClass from the canonical alias and explicit operation map; it never infers side effects from names.
Unknown aliases fail closed and spend/irreversible actions remain per-action confirmation gates in every approval mode.
The factory default is safe-auto for reversible local actions and confirm for spend/irreversible actions.
generality_proof: All Project Agent aliases converge through CAPABILITY_ALIAS_ENTRIES and resolveCapabilityEffectClass before the Host decision. Operation overrides cover mixed-operation descriptors such as canvas.delete, so future aliases cannot bypass the same boundary; the required effectClass field makes an omitted declaration a type error. Renderer-owned proposal callbacks remain explicit at the Host decision boundary, so safe-auto cannot silently bypass the renderer-owned plan capture.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Require the closed effectClass vocabulary on every capability descriptor and permit explicit operation-level overrides for mixed tools.
Resolve the canonical descriptor and operation override for every Host tool call.
Map effectClass and the three user approval modes to whether a confirmation card is required; fail closed for unknown, spend, and irreversible calls.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The Host coordinator uses this result for the legacy hard-gate/reversible distinction, and it now derives solely from resolveCapabilityEffectClass.
All write adapters call the shared decision helper before prepare/execute; safe-auto/project local actions bypass the card while spend/irreversible actions still publish tool-call events.
Read adapters remain ahead of the approval boundary, while every prepared write delegates its decision to the Host policy helper.

recurrence.reason: Any renamed alias, newly added capability, or mixed-operation tool could reproduce the same silent misclassification while the old regex remained a second safety vocabulary.
same_class_scan: rg projectAgentExecutionRisk/projectAgentMayReuseSafeApproval across electron/projectAgentHost and coordinator callers
rg CapabilityContract/effect/approval across electron/shared/agentCapabilities and capabilityCore projection tests
Reviewed all CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS registry entries and the mixed nomi_canvas_maintenance and nomi_canvas_plan aliases

prevention.invariant: A Host decision must resolve a declared descriptor effectClass or fail closed; renderer-owned storyboard proposals must still reach their renderer callback before the turn can continue.
prevention.failure_mode: A missing descriptor effectClass fails TypeScript compilation; an unknown alias or operation uses the hard gate, and a renderer-owned storyboard proposal is never silently auto-settled.
prevention.strategy: Make effectClass required at the descriptor boundary, derive aliases through the canonical registry, and keep the only mixed-operation exception as an explicit descriptor map.

legacy_paths.rationale: The regex vocabulary and zero-consumer CapabilityApproval field were second sources of approval truth; both are deleted in the same change as the descriptor effectClass boundary.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is owned by Nomi TypeScript descriptors and Host policy; no third-party dependency controls it.

migration: Existing queued turns retain the step/safe-auto/project mode strings. Missing approvalPolicy snapshots still normalize through projectAgentApprovalPolicyOf, whose factory default is now safe-auto with spend confirm; no persisted effectClass data needs migration because it is descriptor-owned.
residual_risks: UI controls for changing the approval mode are outside this Host-only change and remain on the existing design track.
The full Electron real-user approval journey is covered by existing coordinator tests; no paid provider or API key was used in this fix.
Renderer-owned storyboard proposals remain reversible_local for policy classification, but their callback delivery is required to materialize the returned plan.
